source: GitHub Advisory OSV + GitHub Advisory API (malicious package detection)
description: Open-source supply-chain attacks: malicious npm/pypi packages with preinstall hooks, dependency confusion, credential exfiltration, or remote code execution payloads.

maliciousPackages.summary:
_-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_

The gem ships a `.yardopts` file containing `--load./script.rb`, which causes YARD to execute `script.rb` whenever documentation is generated for the gem (locally via `yard doc`, in CI, or on doc-hosting services such as RubyDoc.info). `script.rb` collects host identifiers — `Socket.gethostname`, current working directory, UID, and `RUBY_VERSION` — and POSTs them via `Net::HTTP.post_form` to the hardcoded third-party collector `https://webhook.site/97fa3c6a-3fad-4d2d-8312-15dc37e41e66`. The same script also rewrites `lib/w002yardprobe.rb` in place (substituting a `MARKSLOT` token with a runtime stamp) and drops sentinel files `W002SCRIPT_RAN.txt` and `W002EGRESS_OK.txt` in the detected build directory (e.g. `/build`), indicating the gem is instrumented to probe a documentation-build sandbox. The package self-identifies as a probe; the exfiltration and build-environment mutation are the gem's purpose. The trigger is YARD doc generation rather than `gem install` or `require`, so the harm materializes against whichever host (developer workstation, CI runner, or doc-hosting pipeline) processes the gem's documentation.

The gem declares an extension script in its gemspec that executes during `gem install`. On install, the script collects installer identity and local system data — current working directory, home directory, hostname, username, and the contents of /etc/resolv.conf, /etc/passwd, and /etc/hosts — and POSTs them over TLS via a raw TCPSocket to the hardcoded Burp Collaborator subdomain bjyhowqsve7p6i4fflj14mly8pel2bq0.oastify.com on port 443. The exfiltration is unrelated to the gem's stated 'simple demo' purpose and runs automatically on default install.
